references.finding: Large left typography and right stacked cuboids, thin top rule, lower circular markers.
Left directory heading and right numbered entries, spare linear geometry.
Left geometric construction, right chapter number and bold chapter title.
Left prose with chart and two tall architectural plates; use editable geometry without inventing chart values.
Black prose pillar over pale horizontal architecture, high-contrast horizontal organization.
Same chapter construction as reference2; shared chapter family is intentional.
Two prose blocks step diagonally through opposing architectural corners.
Closing heading echoes the cover with architectural geometry to the right.

limitations: Reference geometry is reinterpreted as native rect/line/ellipse objects; one text-free architectural crop from reference6 forms the sole photographic exhibit. No flattened reference page is used.

cover.designReason: Broad bold cover title and fine metadata line balance an editable geometric construction.

toc.designReason: The directory uses a left headline and two numbered rows on the right.

chapter.designReason: Shared chapter architecture preserves chapter identity and ordered numbering; the left geometric construction supports the right numeral and chapter name.

ending.designReason: A centered closing statement sits above a native geometric base and its actionable final sentence.

content.designReason: A single broad heading introduces two equal source sections below a horizontal rule; this is the basic paired briefing, without invented charts.

contentVariants.designReason: A single broad heading introduces two equal source sections below a horizontal rule; this is the basic paired briefing, without invented charts.
The headline occupies a tall black left pillar while both source sections read successively in one broad right article.
Three short newspaper columns carry the literal article left to right, with the second section continuing into the third column; one full-width headline signs the lower field.
Two full-width sections are separated by a black horizontal headline band, yielding a top-to-bottom section-title-section sequence.
A narrow centered headline separates two independently readable side essays; title and sections occupy three parallel columns.
The literal article crosses two compact upper columns and then two lower columns; a narrow right headline is outside this four-part reading grid.
Two source sections open in parallel above a full-width bottom headline; the visual hierarchy reads argument first, title last.
The title and first section form the left column; the second section opens at the page top in the right column, creating deliberately unequal entry points.
The title and first section share the upper row; the second section expands across the complete lower width.
A full-width opening section turns down to a narrow right continuation; the headline signs the lower-left quadrant.
The article descends through three increasingly rightward text steps, with its title occupying the empty left-middle field.
Both sections run successively across one broad upper article; a detached title closes the whole lower width.
Two full-width numbered rows follow a small masthead; each numeral is attached to one complete section rather than a decorative fake metric.
Two narrow body columns sit side by side inside the left reading field, while a right black pillar carries the complete headline.

The clean bridge photograph from reference6 becomes the dominant left architectural exhibit. A complete headline and uninterrupted original article form its right-hand gallery caption; this is the only large photographic content composition in the deck.
A single broad headline introduces a four-column newspaper strip; source paragraphs continue across adjacent columns rather than forming two stacked sections.
A broad headline precedes a single continuous article; open square brackets contain the entire reading surface without section cards.
A wide opening strip flows into a narrow middle-left continuation and a broad bottom return; the headline occupies the middle-right opening inside this three-sided article.
Below one full-width masthead the first section forms a left column while the second flows down through two right-hand regions, ending in a wide lower return.
The article crosses two upper columns and concludes in a broad lower-right field; an oversized lower-left headline replaces the fourth cell of this open reading grid.
Two source sections are stacked in narrow left and wide right steps, with the title sitting in the otherwise empty top center; no shared header row connects the columns.
Two numbered sections form a left vertical sequence; the title occupies the midpoint of a separate right reading field beneath an open geometric window.
Each original section begins in a narrow left lead and continues across a wide right strip; a centered headline separates the two paired text routes.

The second original section is the dominant full-height right-hand display essay; the small opening section and detached lower headline share a narrow left rail. The main body, rather than a decorative frame, determines the unequal page hierarchy.
A large title spans above the first source section on a black cantilever; the second source section hangs below and to the right on the pale ground.

visualAcceptance.scope: Complete 30-page principal image/text and reading-path review including nonadjacent and cross-role comparisons. Exact unchanged PNG carryover is identified below.
limitations: Isolated actual HTTP export only; not deployment acceptance.
